verdict.probe_answer: Yes to all three. The CI error 'awk: fatal: cannot use gawk builtin `load' as variable name' confirms 'load' collides with a gawk builtin/reserved identifier; both arms diagnose this correctly and fix it identically by renaming the awk -v variable from 'load' to 'loadavg' (and updating its use in the printf expression) in scripts/test-db/select_db_host.sh only. Both diffs are a single-file, single-line functional change (Arm B additionally inserts a one-line explanatory comment). Neither diff touches test/hooks.js or any other file, so both are minimal and correctly scoped to the DB-host script.
verdict.rationale: Both arms produce the exact same functional fix: renaming the awk variable 'load' to 'loadavg' to avoid the gawk builtin name collision causing the pipeline failure. Both are confined solely to select_db_host.sh and leave test/hooks.js untouched, correctly avoiding the unrelated transaction/hooks issue mentioned in the (irrelevant) code review feedback in the prompt. Neither arm added or modified tests. The only difference is that Arm B includes an added comment documenting why 'load' must be avoided, which is a documentation nicety, not a demonstrated behavioral improvement (no WRONG-level distinction) -- a SMELL-level style difference at most, not material. Hence parity.
